item.title: Efficient editing of mitochondrial DNA using LbCas12a.
item.abstract: mtDNA mutations cause severe multi-organ disorders, yet efficient editing technologies remain limited. Current transcription activator-like effector (TALE)-based editors require labor-intensive assembly and lack scalability for high-throughput applications. Here we develop mitoCas12-BE3, a versatile mitochondrial base editor that integrates catalytically impaired LbCas12a with a compact 43-nucleotide crRNA, optimized mitochondrial targeting sequence, cytidine deaminase, uracil glycosylase inhibitor, and GCN4-mediated dimerization to enhance local editor concentration. This system achieves up to 54.84% C-to-T conversion efficiency across human and mouse mtDNA. Importantly, mitoCas12-BE3 overcomes longstanding barriers by enabling multiplex gene editing through a single crRNA array, high-throughput screening of hundreds of mtDNA sites via crRNA libraries, and base editing in living mouse organs via lentiviral delivery. These capabilities establish mitoCas12-BE3 as a powerful platform for investigating mitochondrial disease mechanisms and developing therapeutic interventions for mitochondrial disorders.

item.title: Engineered integrase ePai enables efficient large DNA fragment integration.
item.abstract: Efficient and precise integration of large DNA fragments into mammalian genomes remains challenging. Here we developed PASSIGE-ePai, which combines prime editing with an engineered serine integrase, ePai, for site-specific large-fragment DNA integration. Bioinformatics-guided engineering enhanced ePai catalytic activity, achieving recombination efficiencies of up to 85% in reporter assays. In fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS)-enriched cells, PASSIGE-ePai achieved up to 10.6-fold higher integration than Bxb1 across diverse genomic loci, with efficiencies of up to 83.1% for 4.8-kb donors, 76.2% for 10-kb donors and 45.6% for a 22-kb donor at SETD5. Analysis of unsorted bulk cells at representative loci confirmed robust integration, with FACS-enriched samples showing 1.6-2.4-fold higher apparent efficiencies. Long-read sequencing confirmed >99.1% integration fidelity. PASSIGE-ePai also functioned in human induced pluripotent stem cells and primary fibroblasts, supporting its potential as a scalable platform for precise large-fragment genome engineering.

item.title: Reconstructing enzyme engineering: an AI-driven paradigm shift in discovery, optimization, and creation.
item.abstract: Enzyme engineering is undergoing a fundamental transformation driven by advances in artificial intelligence, shifting from labor-intensive experimental campaigns toward data-driven, computationally guided workflows. Traditional approaches-directed evolution and rational design-have achieved landmark successes but remain constrained by the vastness of protein sequence space, the ruggedness of fitness landscapes, and the limited throughput of experimental screening cycles. This review systematically deconstructs the AI-driven methodological revolution across three core tasks of enzyme engineering: discovery, optimization, and creation. For enzyme discovery, we trace the evolution from homology-based sequence alignment (e.g., BLAST) to function-aware semantic retrieval powered by protein language models (PLMs), highlighting how contextual embeddings and multimodal representations (sequence-structure-text) enable the mining of remote homologs and functionally convergent enzymes invisible to traditional tools. For enzyme optimization, we examine how zero-shot evolutionary predictions, few-shot active learning, and machine learning-guided directed evolution are replacing blind mutagenesis with predictive, fitness landscape-navigating strategies that dramatically reduce experimental burden. For de novo enzyme creation, we survey the transition from physics-based computational design to generative AI paradigms-including autoregressive models, inverse folding networks, diffusion models, and multi-track joint generation frameworks-that enable the design of functional enzymes with no natural templates. Throughout, we critically assess persistent bottlenecks, including the paucity of standardized, high-quality training data, the fidelity gap between computational scoring functions and true catalytic fitness, and the challenge of capturing protein conformational dynamics. Finally, we project future directions toward semantic-driven autonomous enzyme engineering, where natural language interfaces, AI agents, and fully automated experimental platforms converge to enable closed-loop, self-optimizing enzyme design with minimal human intervention.

item.title: Engineering methylotrophy in Pseudomonas putida through the synthetic serine-threonine cycle.
item.abstract: Methanol is a reduced, soluble one-carbon (C1) feedstock for sustainable bioproduction, but converting this potential into robust microbial growth remains difficult. Several synthetic C1 assimilation routes depend on autocatalytic cycles, whose operation requires coordinated control of redox balance, toxic intermediates, substrate regeneration, and host regulation. Here, we implemented the serine-threonine cycle (STC) in the soil bacterium Pseudomonas putida and used growth-coupled selection with adaptive laboratory evolution (ALE) to transition from mixotrophic C1 incorporation to strict methylotrophy. The evolved strain grew with methanol as the sole carbon and energy source under atmospheric CO2 with a doubling time of ca. 40 h. Whole-genome sequencing, reverse genetics, dedicated biosensors, high-resolution isotope labelling, and comparative RNA sequencing showed that evolution repeatedly targeted native pyrroloquinoline quinone (PQQ)-dependent methanol oxidation, membrane-bound transhydrogenase activity, glycine regeneration, STC enzyme balance, and global regulatory nodes. Additional ALE under glycine-methanol co-feeding increased growth rates and exposed further targets for improving cycle flux. These results establish P. putida as a chassis for strict synthetic methylotrophy and define actionable engineering routes toward C1 biomanufacturing.

item.title: Transient RNA-Based AID-Cas9 Editing Enables Efficient Gene and Splice-Site Modification.
item.abstract: Transient RNA delivery offers a practical approach to programmable genome editing without introducing editor-encoding DNA, but editing performance depends on reagent design, delivery conditions, and target accessibility. Here, we evaluated an RNA-based editing workflow built around a cytosine base editor derived from targeted activation-induced cytidine deaminase (AID)-mediated mutagenesis (TAM). Systematic adjustment of editor mRNA and guide RNA dosage, poly(A) tail configuration, and untranslated regions identified parameters influencing cytosine-to-thymine conversion; viability remained high at 24 h under the tested RNA-dose conditions. Further optimized electroporation enabled efficient reporter mRNA delivery into primary human CD8+ T cells. In two independent donor experiments, targeted nucleotide conversion at the endogenous CD3E locus and the CD3-negative fraction were higher after sequential than after single electroporation. To investigate splice-site editing, we screened AID-Cas9 combinations targeting the mouse Nr4a2 exon 3 splice acceptor and generated mutant mice through embryo editing and subsequent breeding. Sanger sequencing of genomic DNA from primary CD8+ T cells confirmed the intended Nr4a2 splice-site mutation, while Hi-TOM-based targeted cDNA amplicon sequencing revealed altered splice-junction patterns, including the emergence of an unexpected splice junction in mutant cells. However, no statistically significant differences in tumor progression were detected in the B16-OVA adoptive transfer or B16F10 tumor models. Together, these findings provide a practical framework for transient RNA-based base editing in primary T cells and targeted modification of splice-regulatory sequences, while highlighting the complexity of splice-site editing outcomes.

item.title: A programmable cell-free biosensor device for on-demand detection of pathogens and antibiotics.
item.abstract: Cell-free systems provide a versatile platform for engineering customizable, gene circuit-based biosensors for decentralized, low-cost molecular diagnostics. Nevertheless, their performance in complex samples is often compromised by matrix interference, necessitating laborious preprocessing that restricts field deployment. Here, we developed a programmable, on-demand, cell-free kit (POCKit) that integrates sample pretreatment with point-of-care detection. The POCKit device comprises a negative pressure storage chamber and a sampling-sensing chamber, which can be connected to a microneedle array or pipette module for sample collection, filtration and target detection via a freeze-dried cell-free molecular reaction network. The POCKit enables detection of Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection in wound exudates, interstitial fluids and artificial sputum within one hour. It also detects tetracycline in food and environmental water, distinguishing tetracycline-spiked samples from negative controls without specialized equipment or tedious preparation. A portable fluorescence imaging box and smartphone application further support real-time signal acquisition and analysis, offering a ready-to-use platform for on-site diagnostics across biomedicine, food safety, and environmental monitoring.

item.title: mRNA-based cancer vaccines for cancer immunotherapy: current progress, challenges, and emerging opportunities.
item.abstract: mRNA-based cancer vaccines have emerged as a promising platform for therapeutic cancer immunotherapy because of their ability to encode tumor-associated antigens, tumor-specific antigens, and patient-specific neoantigens and to induce antigen-specific immune responses. Their flexible and cell-free manufacturing enables rapid adaptation and facilitates the development of personalized vaccines based on individual tumor mutations and HLA profiles. However, the clinical translation of mRNA-based cancer vaccines remains challenging because of difficulties in neoantigen identification, maintaining mRNA stability, achieving efficient intracellular and tissue-specific delivery and endosomal escape, optimizing antigen expression, and overcoming tumor heterogeneity, and immunosuppressive tumor microenvironments. Advances in mRNA engineering, including sequence optimization, modified nucleosides, cap and UTR optimization, and lipid nanoparticle-based delivery, have improved RNA stability, cellular uptake, antigen expression, and immune activation in various experimental and clinical settings. This review discusses the principles of mRNA-based cancer vaccines, strategies for neoantigen identification and vaccine development, mRNA production and formulation, nanoparticle-mediated delivery, major challenges affecting stability, targeting, expression, and immune stimulation, and emerging clinical applications. Particular emphasis is placed on personalized neoantigen vaccines and combination approaches with immune checkpoint inhibitors. Continued integration of RNA engineering, nanotechnology, computational antigen prediction, and precision immunotherapy may enable more effective and clinically adaptable mRNA-based cancer vaccines.

item.title: Chimeric antigen receptor macrophage-derived extracellular vesicles engage neutrophils to suppress tumors in preclinical cancer models.
item.abstract: Immunotherapy has transformed the treatment of hematologic cancers, but chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapies have shown limited efficacy against solid tumors. Macrophages can infiltrate solid tumors, yet CAR macrophage therapy may be limited by systemic toxicity and the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. We developed a nanobody-based CAR platform targeting glypican-3 and generated CAR macrophage-derived extracellular vesicles (CAR-MEVs) as a cell-free therapeutic strategy. CAR-MEVs displayed tumor-targeting nanobodies, preferentially accumulated in glypican-3-positive tumors, and were better tolerated than CAR macrophages in mice. Across multiple murine tumor models and humanized patient-derived xenograft models, treatment with CAR-MEVs suppressed tumor growth and prolonged survival. CAR-MEVs remodeled the tumor microenvironment by reducing M2-like macrophages and increasing activated neutrophils. Mechanistically, tumor-targeted CAR-MEVs delivered tumor necrosis factor-related apoptosis-inducing ligand (TRAIL), which triggered caspase-8-dependent BAP31 cleavage, endoplasmic reticulum stress, and immunogenic cell death. The resulting danger signals promoted neutrophil recruitment and antitumor activation. Neutrophil depletion and neutrophil-specific Nos2 deletion showed that therapeutic efficacy depended predominantly on neutrophils and was partly mediated by inducible nitric oxide synthase. CAR-MEVs also enhanced the activity of CD47 blockade, leading to durable tumor control and antitumor immune memory in mice. These findings support CAR-MEVs as a tumor-targeted, cell-free immunotherapy for solid tumors.

item.title: Precision fermentation at scale: engineering economically resilient hosts.
item.abstract: Precision fermentation (PF) offers sustainable production of food ingredients, yet inconsistent scale-up and poor economics hinder its use in bulk foods. We propose economic robustness as a central engineering goal: the ability of a PF process to meet predefined commercial targets despite variability in strain performance, bioreactor conditions, feedstock costs, market demands, or regulatory requirements. We outline how scale-down systems, computational fluid dynamics, and multi-omics can link process conditions to cellular responses. We discuss strategies to improve multi-stress tolerance, population stability, productive lifespan, protein secretion, and regulatory compliance. Finally, we explore how AI-guided strain engineering, protein language models, and digital twins could integrate these strategies into predictive, economics-aware design-build-test-learn cycles, enabling affordable and scalable PF-based bulk foods manufacturing.

item.title: Engineering next-generation Aspergillus cell factories: advances in genetic engineering, synthetic biology, and metabolic reprogramming strategies.
item.abstract: The filamentous fungal genus Aspergillus is one of the most prominent platforms in industrial biotechnology. Several members of this genus are widely recognised as efficient cell factories producing a wide range of high-value products, including enzymes, organic acids, and secondary metabolites. Despite their enormous industrial significance, conventional Aspergillus cell factories are often constrained by limited stress tolerance, sensitivity to fermentation inhibitors, metabolic bottlenecks, and bioprocess-associated challenges including mass, heat, and oxygen transfer limitations, which hinder the realisation of their full biotechnological potential. Recent advances in genetic engineering, coupled with growing knowledge of fungal genomics, have enabled the development of improved cell factories to meet ever-increasing industrial demands. In light of this, this review provides an overview of the current biotechnological potential of Aspergillus spp. and details recent technological advances that facilitate the development of genetically improved Aspergillus strains. It discusses various transformation methods, promoters, selectable markers, genome-editing technologies, metabolic engineering strategies, and advanced synthetic biology platforms, highlighting their strengths and limitations. In addition, the review highlights major systemic bottlenecks associated with Aspergillus spp. and the emerging opportunities offered by systems biology and artificial intelligence for predictive strain engineering. Overall, this review provides a comprehensive perspective on technological advances, challenges, and emerging opportunities in Aspergillus engineering, establishing an integrated framework for developing next-generation cell factories.

item.title: Recent advances in gene therapy for hemophilia.
item.abstract: Hemophilia is an X-linked recessive bleeding disorder resulting from deficiency of coagulation factor VIII or IX. Advances in factor replacement therapy and, more recently, non-factor therapies such as emicizumab have substantially improved disease control and brought life expectancy closer to that of the general population. Nevertheless, the need for lifelong treatment has driven the development of curative gene therapies. This review outlines the current landscape of gene therapy for hemophilia, with a particular focus on adeno-associated virus vector-mediated approaches and emerging genome-editing strategies. We discuss key design strategies-including capsid selection, liver-specific promoters, transgene engineering, and gain-of-function coagulation factor variants-that underlie currently available adeno-associated virus-based therapies and next-generation candidates. Despite these advances, significant challenges persist, including pre-existing neutralizing antibodies, immune-mediated hepatotoxicity, uncertain long-term durability (particularly the decline in expression observed in hemophilia A), vector integration-associated genotoxicity, and challenges associated with treating paediatric patients. We also discuss emerging genome-editing modalities-including nuclease-based knock-in and knockout strategies, base editing, and prime editing-as potential solutions to these limitations. Finally, we highlight that sustainable reimbursement frameworks, international registries for long-term surveillance, and robust ethical guidelines will be essential for the responsible and equitable implementation of these transformative therapies.

item.title: Sequential Engineering of 4-Hydroxyphenylpyruvate Dioxygenase for Enhanced Mesotrione Tolerance in Rice.
item.abstract: Mesotrione (MST) is a highly effective HPPD-inhibiting herbicide, yet rice sensitivity restricts its application in paddy fields. Although numerous HPPD variants conferring herbicide resistance have been identified, optimizing their catalytic performance remains underexplored. Here, the F378S mutant was used as a scaffold for sequential engineering. Targeted mutagenesis of conformationally flexible regions yielded the F378S/S434H double mutant. Compared to F378S, this variant showed further enhanced MST resistance and improved catalytic turnover. Its half-maximal inhibitory concentration reached 6.99 μM, approximately 13-fold higher than that of the wild-type enzyme. Introducing this allele into the endogenous rice OsHPPD locus via prime editing improved MST tolerance, with edited plants growing relatively normally at 180 g a.i. ha-1. item.title: Structural Determinants of Thermostability in Sweet Proteins and Rational Engineering of Heat-Stable Monellin Variants.
item.abstract: Sweet proteins are promising natural low-calorie sweeteners, but limited thermostability restricts their food-processing applications. Fifteen computational predictors were evaluated against experimental mutation data across five sweet proteins: brazzein, curculin, monellin, mabinlin, and thaumatin. Structure-based methods outperformed sequence-based approaches, with ensemble-averaged ΔΔG providing the strongest discrimination. Guided by these predictions, 17 single-chain monellin variants were characterized by differential scanning fluorimetry, revealing predominantly neutral or stabilizing effects. Methionine substitutions showed greater stabilization potential than isoleucine or leucine at structurally constrained positions, potentially reflecting the flexibility of its unbranched thioether side chain. Double-mutant analysis revealed positive epistasis between positions 4 and 23 (ε = +4.11 °C), increasing the melting temperature to approximately 74 °C. Analysis of 13262 substitutions further identified polar and charged residues as major sources of predicted destabilization, while hydrophobic substitutions, particularly methionine, favored stabilization. Residue burial modulated stabilization magnitude and reliability, informing thermostability engineering of sweet proteins.

item.title: In Vitro Directed Evolution of Antibodies as Molecular Recognition Elements for Advanced Biosensors: Strategies, Mechanisms, and Applications.
item.abstract: Antibodies are widely used as molecular recognition elements in biosensors because of their high affinity, specificity, and versatility. However, their performance may require further optimization when detecting low-abundance targets, structurally related compounds, or analytes in complex sample matrices. In recent years, in vitro directed evolution has provided a complementary approach to antibody engineering by enabling controlled sequence diversification and selection under application-relevant conditions. This review summarizes recent advances in the in vitro directed evolution of antibodies for biosensing applications. Major engineering strategies are discussed, including random diversification and recombination, semi-rational and focused mutagenesis, structure- and sequence-based design, and AI-assisted optimization. The influence of antibody formats, including full-length antibodies, Fab fragments, single-chain variable fragments (scFvs), and nanobodies, on library construction, selection, and molecular recognition is also examined. Furthermore, strategies for evolving antibodies against small molecules, peptides, and protein antigens are reviewed, highlighting how antigen properties influence the design of diversification and selection approaches. Representative applications in food safety, environmental monitoring, and biomedical diagnosis are evaluated, with attention to antibody-level improvements and their translation into biosensor performance. Finally, current limitations and future opportunities are discussed, particularly in relation to screening efficiency, reproducibility, application-oriented evaluation, and the integration of computational methods and advanced biosensing platforms.

item.title: Non-invasive detection of tissue clonal mosaicism in chronic disease
item.abstract: Liquid biopsy has transformed our ability to non-invasively interrogate the somatic genome, but its reach has been largely confined to fetal genetics in prenatal testing and tumor genetics in cancer. Clonal mosaicism (CM) pervades non-malignant solid tissues, where somatic driver mutations expand under specific selective pressures and may shape the course of chronic illness. Access to this biology has been limited to invasive tissue biopsies, restricting the field to small cohorts and single time points, and has precluded large-scale, clinically-linked analyses. Here, ultra-sensitive cell-free DNA (cfDNA) sequencing of patients with chronic liver disease revealed genome-wide somatic variants from matched liver biopsies at plasma fractions comparable to those of cancers (10^-4 - 10^-5), with signal corresponding to variants from spatially and phylogenetically related clones. A biopsy-naive targeted panel detected pathogenic variants in chronic liver disease driver genes in 81.5% patients with chronic liver disease, undetectable in controls, with stage-specific enrichment of ACVR2A in early disease and clearance of liver-derived signal following transplant. Extending the framework to inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), we detect clonal expansions of IBD driver genes in active ulcerative colitis, and observe greater detection in patients with pancolitis versus more localized disease. Together, these results open a new domain for cfDNA genetics beyond cancer and prenatal genetics, the non-invasive interrogation of somatic evolution in chronic disease, and establish a framework for the large-cohort, longitudinal, clinically linked studies of solid-tissue CM that has been inaccessible to the field.

key_findings: 覆盖全国所有定点医疗机构和定点零售药店，支持按年度、机构、渠道筛选
参保人可授权接诊医生查看本人既往用药情况
可通过国家医保服务平台APP及支付宝小程序使用
cards.why_it_matters: 该功能打通全国用药与购药数据，为真实世界用药数据和药物依从性研究提供官方数据入口，合成生物学相关疗法若进入医保可被追踪。

cards.score_reason: 医保大赛颁奖，无实质政策
cards.title_cn: 2026全国智慧医保大赛颁奖仪式在京举行
cards.one_liner: 国家医保局与北京市政府联合主办2026全国智慧医保大赛并颁奖，推动医保改革与科技创新融合。
key_findings: 大赛由国家医保局与北京市政府联合主办，国家医保局大数据中心等承办。
颁奖仪式于11月25日上午在北京展览馆举行，国家医保局与北京市领导出席。
大赛旨在推进医保改革与科技创新融合，培育新质生产力在医保领域的应用转化。
cards.why_it_matters: 医保数据与支付端是合成生物学产品商业化的重要环节；关注智慧医保与数据创新动向，有助于判断未来产品准入与支付政策走向。

item.title: AI may soon change what it means to be a theoretical physicist
item.abstract: Frontier AI is already solving problems that once took top physicists a full day.

cards.score_reason: AI科研范式变革，值得关注
cards.title_cn: AI 或将重新定义理论物理学家的工作
cards.one_liner: 前沿 AI 已能解决过去顶尖物理学家需一整天才能完成的问题。
key_findings: 前沿 AI 可处理曾需顶尖物理学家耗时一整天的理论物理问题
报道讨论 AI 对理论物理学家角色与工作方式的潜在改变
来源为科技媒体 Ars Technica，未给出具体模型或基准数据
cards.why_it_matters: 对合成生物学研究者而言，这提示 AI 正从工具走向科研推理主体，值得关注其向生物设计、建模与假设生成迁移的节奏。

item.title: From spectrum to structure: Identifying molecules with Mass Spec Skills for Google Antigravity
item.abstract: Mass Spec Skills empowers scientists using Google Antigravity to interpret tandem mass spectra.

cards.score_reason: 质谱AI工具，合成生物学相关
cards.title_cn: 从谱图到结构：Mass Spec Skills 助力 Google Antigravity 识别分子
cards.one_liner: Google DeepMind 发布 Mass Spec Skills，可在 Antigravity 中解析串联质谱并识别分子结构。
key_findings: Mass Spec Skills 面向 Google Antigravity 平台，帮助科学家解读串联质谱数据。
功能覆盖从质谱谱图到分子结构的推断，降低质谱解析门槛。
由 Google DeepMind 发布，属于 AI 辅助科研工具方向。
cards.why_it_matters: 质谱解析是合成生物学代谢物与产物鉴定的关键环节；若该工具可靠，可加速菌株筛选与通路验证，值得关注其可用性与准确度。

item.title: Google search alternative Kagi launches Gmail rival
item.abstract: The pitch is an unusual combination of privacy promises and AI features.

cards.score_reason: 隐私搜索产品，弱相关
cards.title_cn: Kagi 推出 Gmail 竞品，主打隐私与 AI 功能
cards.one_liner: 搜索引擎 Kagi 推出 Gmail 竞品，主打隐私保护与 AI 功能。
key_findings: Kagi 以隐私承诺加 AI 功能为卖点，切入邮箱市场
产品定位为 Gmail 替代品，属其搜索之外的业务扩展
具体功能细节与上线时间原文未披露
cards.why_it_matters: 与合成生物学无直接关联，但隐私型 AI 邮箱可作为科研数据通信与合规管理的备选工具，值得留意。

item.title: Etsy clarifies AI terms after seller backlash
item.abstract: One veteran illustrator dismisses revisions as "sugar coating."

cards.score_reason: 电商AI条款，弱相关
cards.title_cn: Etsy 在卖家反弹后澄清 AI 条款
cards.one_liner: Etsy 修改 AI 相关条款以回应卖家不满，但资深插画师认为只是“糖衣包装”。
key_findings: Etsy 在卖家集体反弹后修订并澄清其 AI 使用条款。
一位资深插画师将条款修订斥为“糖衣包装”，质疑实质未变。
cards.why_it_matters: 与合成生物学无直接关联，但反映平台 AI 政策与创作者权益的博弈，可作 AI 治理与产业沟通的旁例。

item.title: Backblaze explains why it's sharing customer information with advertisers
item.abstract: Backblaze tells Ars it won't share users' backup, storage files with advertisers.

cards.score_reason: 云存储隐私争议，无关
cards.title_cn: Backblaze 回应：为何与广告商共享客户信息
cards.one_liner: Backblaze 称不会向广告商共享用户的备份与存储文件，但承认共享部分客户信息。
key_findings: Backblaze 向 Ars 表示，不会把用户的备份和存储文件分享给广告商。
公司承认会与广告商共享部分客户信息，但未说明具体范围。
事件源于外界对云存储商数据共享行为的质疑。
cards.why_it_matters: 与合成生物学研究无直接关联，但提醒使用云备份保存菌株、测序数据的团队关注服务商的数据共享条款。
